We need to answer using policy excerpts. The question: "I can't find the SSO sign-in option on the login page — was my account actually provisioned by the identity provider sync?" This is about SSO sign-in option missing, asking if account was provisioned. According to DOC-010 parts: SSO sign-in appears only for email domain configured and after identity provider sync created account. Admin can check in Settings → People; absence means sync hasn't created it yet. Also new hire may be signing before sync or account not exist on identity provider side. So answer: explain that sign-in option appears only after sync, you can check in Settings → People, if not there then sync hasn't created it yet. Possibly advise to wait for next sync or ensure account exists on IdP. Provide short answer.

We can answer directly, no need to escalate. Use post_reply.

function.arguments: {"message":"The SSO sign‑in button only shows up for users whose account has already been created by the identity‑provider sync. If your account isn’t listed in **Settings → People** (SSO‑provisioned accounts are marked with the identity provider name), the sync hasn’t created it yet. This can happen if you’re a new hire signing in before the next scheduled sync or if the account doesn’t exist on the IdP side. You’ll need to wait for the sync to run or have an admin verify the account exists in the IdP and then re‑run the sync."}
